 Print 'Hanuman Ansh' producer Anupriya Nagar calls Ranbir Kapoor's 'Ramayana' work a 'phenomenal job'; picks 'Barfi!' over 'Tamasha' as her favourite film of actor Anupriya Nagar, the 21-year-old producer of ‘Hanuman Ansh’, has opened up about her love for Ranbir Kapoor and her excitement for Nitesh Tiwari ’s ‘ Ramayana ’. The self-declared fan also named the one film of the actor that she likes the most. Anupriya Nagar on Ranbir Kapoor's performance in 'Ramayana'
 In a chat with Radio City, the young producer said she has followed Ranbir Kapoor’s work since her early years and can’t wait to see him as Lord Ram. Anupriya Nagar said, “He is a wonderful actor. Main toh bachpan se hi dekhti aa rahi hoon unki movies (I have been watching his films since childhood) aur main bahut excited hoon ki main unko Ram ji ke role mein dekhungi (and I am very excited to see him play Lord Ram). I think it is also a miracle ki kaise Hanuman ji pehle aaye hain aur phir Ram ji aa rahe hain (that Hanuman ji came first and now Ram ji is arriving). Jo bhi maine abhi tak dekha hai (whatever I have seen so far), phenomenal job." Her favourite Ranbir Kapoor film
 When asked to pick her best-loved titles from his career, Anupriya Nagar went with ‘Barfi!’ and also gave a shout-out to Imtiaz Ali’s ‘Tamasha’. She explained, “Barfi!, but I also like Tamasha, kyunki humare jo problems hain (because the struggles and issues we face), for the first time unhone ek film ke zariye bataya hai (were conveyed through a film for the first time). Barfi! of course, but also Tamasha.” What next after ‘Hanuman Ansh’?
 Given the success of her debut, the producer was also asked whether she would now move towards mainstream commercial cinema or stay with the genre that has worked for her. She made it clear that her path is set for now. Join conversation

 She added, “As of now, mera yahi uddeshya hai ki main spiritual films banaun (my aim is to make spiritual films), because abhi yahi focus hai ke main bachchon tak yeh leke jaun (because my focus right now is to take these stories to children). Humaari jo sanskriti, values aur history hai Bharat ki (our culture, values and history as Indians), main nahi chahti ki abhi ka yug jaane, par 10 saal baad ka yug bhi jaane (I don’t want only the present generation to know about them, but the generation 10 years from now as well). ” ‘Ramayana’ box office update
 Meanwhile, the Nitesh Tiwari film is enjoying a strong run in theatres after completing two weeks. According to trade estimates, it is set to become the second fastest film to enter the Rs 650 crore Hindi net club on day 15. It has also become the second Hindi film of the year, after ‘Dhurandhar 2’, to add Rs 200 crore in its second week. As no big release is lined up this Friday, ‘Ramayana’ may break a few more records soon.
